texts.li: Somebody carved a line down the middle of the dining table this week. {A_nameDef} eats on one side of it and {B_nameDef} on the other, and the rest of the colony has had to pick a side to sit on. Neither of them can say anymore how the feud started.\n\n{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} came to the council together, which has never happened before. Each wants it ended for good, and each has a clear idea of who should lose.

The feud between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} has spread to the rest of the colony. Work crews are picked by side, jokes are told at one or the other's expense, and the dining room goes quiet whenever both of them walk in.\n\nBoth have demanded that the council settle it. {A_nameDef} wants {B_nameDef} put in {B_possessive} place, and {B_nameDef} wants the same for {A_nameDef}.

li.label: Settle it in the yard, by the rules, once
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} fought it out in the yard under the council's rules, and both swore to let it drop afterward. They came away bruised and limping, and so far they have mostly kept their word.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} fought it out in the yard under the council's rules. Both claim to have won, and both have started training for the rematch.

li.label: Keep them apart: separate shifts, separate meals
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now work different hours, eat at different times and only meet by accident. The rest of the colony had its week rearranged to make it work, and isn't happy about it.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} were kept apart for nine whole days, until a narrow doorway and bad timing put them face to face.

li.label: Make them teach each other their trades
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent a week teaching each other their trades through gritted teeth. Both learned something, and by the end of it they could get through a lesson without shouting.
li.riskOutcome: The lessons lasted one morning. {B_nameDef} called {A_nameDef} hopeless, {A_nameDef} hit {B_objective} in the nose, and that was the end of the lessons.

li.label: Tell them to grow up
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to settle it like adults. The line down the middle of the colony is still there, and it is getting deeper.
li.riskOutcome: The council told them to grow up. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} took that as permission and settled it with their fists across the dinner table.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have become the kind of friends who finish each other's sentences and steal each other's food. For weeks they've been swapping shifts behind the council's back to work together, and the roster no longer makes sense to anyone else.\n\nNow they're asking openly for the same shifts and the same crews, for good. The people stuck covering the gaps want to know why a friendship should earn anyone special treatment.

Every time the council posts a roster, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} rearrange it so they end up side by side. The work still gets done, more or less, so no one has complained out loud yet.\n\n{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} would like it made official: same hours, same jobs, no more sneaking. A few of the others would like it stopped.

li.label: Let them work together
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now work every shift together and talk through all of it. The work is fine, though the people working next to them have heard more than they wanted to.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now work every shift together, and get about half as much done, because most of every shift is talking.

li.label: Give them the night watch, together
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} got their wish on the night watch, which no one else wanted. They're happy with the arrangement, and tired most of the day.

li.label: Keep the roster as it is
li.outcome: The council kept the roster as it was. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} still find each other at meals, and glare at the roster on the way past.
li.riskOutcome: The council kept the roster as it was, and {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} went on swapping shifts behind its back. The roster is now so tangled that people keep turning up for the wrong jobs.

li.label: Split them up on purpose
li.outcome: The council put {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} at opposite ends of the day, to keep the colony from turning into cliques. They leave each other notes now, and the notes are getting longer.
li.riskOutcome: The council put {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} on opposite shifts, so they started meeting in secret in the small hours. They're closer than ever, and short on sleep.

texts.li: Rats got into the storeroom last week and ate through a good part of the food. The colony blamed a broken latch. It came out today that {A_nameDef} left the door open that night, and that {B_nameDef} knew and made up the story about the latch.\n\n{A_nameDef} is ashamed of it. {B_nameDef} isn't, and says {B_pronoun} would do the same for a friend again. The colony wants to know which of them the council blames.

The fire that blackened the workshop last week "started on its own," according to {B_nameDef}, who was very convincing about it. In fact it started with {A_nameDef}, a lamp left burning and a long nap.\n\n{A_nameDef} has owned up. {B_nameDef} hasn't apologized for the lie and doesn't plan to. The colony is waiting to see whether the council punishes the mistake, the lie, or neither.

li.label: Punish them both
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are both working off the punishment, side by side, in disgrace. Sharing it has only brought them closer.

li.label: Punish {A_nameDef} for the mistake
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is working off the damage. {B_nameDef} got off free, and seems uncomfortable about it.

li.label: Punish {B_nameDef} for the lie
li.outcome: The council ruled that a mistake is a mistake but a lie is a choice. {B_nameDef} is working off the punishment, and {A_nameDef} can't look {B_objective} in the eye.

li.label: Let it go
li.outcome: The council let it go. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are relieved. The others have started checking the latches themselves.
li.riskOutcome: The council let it go. A few days later {A_nameDef} slipped up again, and {B_nameDef} was halfway through a new story before anyone checked.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} stood together the last time the colony was attacked, and they haven't stopped talking about it since. They want a night set aside to remember the fight properly: a fire, a real meal, the whole story told start to end, and a drink for everyone who bled.\n\nIt would cost about {COUNT} raw food and a day of everyone's work. {A_nameDef} says some things are worth a day. {B_nameDef} says the ones who bled deserve at least that.

Since the last attack, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have been close in the way only people who've been shot at together are. They've come to the council asking for a remembrance night for the fight, with food, a fire, and everyone there to hear it.\n\nThe cooks have worked out the cost, about {COUNT} raw food, and aren't pleased. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} say that's what the stores are for.

li.label: Hold the remembrance night
li.outcome: The colony sat up late while {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} told the story of the fight, which grew with every telling. It was nearly dawn before people went to bed.

li.label: Allow speeches, but no feast
li.outcome: The council allowed speeches after dinner, and nothing more. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} said their piece to a room that kept glancing at the door.

li.label: Only those who fought may come
li.outcome: The ones who fought held their own night behind a closed door. The rest of the colony could hear them laughing through the wall.

li.label: No. The stores are for the living
li.outcome: The council said no. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} drank to the fight alone, out by the wall, and haven't been as quick to volunteer since.
li.riskOutcome: The council said no, so {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} held the remembrance anyway, after dark, on food taken from the stores. A good number of people turned up.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} stood up at dinner and announced that {A_nameDef} has been stealing silver from the stores. {B_nameDef} has no proof, only a feeling, a rough count of the silver and a long history of hating {A_nameDef}.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants {A_nameDef} punished. {A_nameDef} wants {B_nameDef} to take it back, in front of the same people who heard it.

A knife, some silver and a good pair of boots have gone missing this month. {B_nameDef} says {A_nameDef} took them, and says it loudly and often, though no one else has seen anything.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants the council to act. {A_nameDef} points out that {B_nameDef} would blame {A_objective} for the weather if it rained.

li.label: Search {A_nameDef}'s things
li.outcome: The council turned out {A_nameDef}'s belongings with a crowd watching and found nothing worth mentioning. {A_nameDef} will not forget who asked for it.
li.riskOutcome: The council searched {A_nameDef}'s things and found forty silver hidden under the bedroll. The silver went back to the stores, {A_nameDef} is working off the theft, and {B_nameDef} hasn't stopped talking about it.

li.label: Take {B_nameDef}'s word for it
li.outcome: On {B_nameDef}'s word alone, {A_nameDef} is working off a theft no one saw. {A_nameDef}'s friends think it was badly unfair, and have told {B_nameDef} so.

li.label: Throw the case out
li.outcome: The council threw the accusation out for want of proof. {B_nameDef} has started keeping a ledger of the silver, and stares at {A_nameDef} while writing in it.
li.riskOutcome: The council threw the accusation out for want of proof. A week later forty more silver went missing, and {B_nameDef} has been saying "I told you so" ever since.

li.label: Make {B_nameDef} take it back in public
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} took it back at dinner, through clenched teeth, in front of the same people who heard the accusation. The apology wasn't sincere, but {A_nameDef} was satisfied with it.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} began the public apology, got three words in, and turned it into a punch.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} used to be inseparable. Lately {A_nameDef} has fallen in with a different crowd, and {B_nameDef} eats alone, goes to bed early and tells anyone who asks that it's fine.\n\n{B_nameDef} finally came to the council, embarrassed, to ask for help. {A_nameDef} doesn't see a problem, since people are allowed more than one friend.

{B_nameDef} has started turning up wherever {A_nameDef} is, too casually, and leaving too quickly when {A_nameDef}'s new friends arrive. The others have noticed, and it's hard to watch.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants the old friendship back and doesn't know how to ask. {A_nameDef} wants to choose {A_possessive} own company without a council meeting about it.

li.label: Ask {A_nameDef} to make time for {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has been setting evenings aside for {B_nameDef}, on the council's advice. The first few were stiff, but the two of them have started laughing together again.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} found out who went to the council. The evenings set aside for {B_nameDef} have been very short and very quiet.

li.label: Bring {B_nameDef} into the new crowd
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} brought {B_nameDef} along to the new crowd's evenings. {B_nameDef} has a table to sit at again, though some of the new crowd aren't sure they want {B_objective} there.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} brought {B_nameDef} along to the new crowd's evenings, where {B_nameDef} was politely ignored all night. It was worse than eating alone.

li.label: Keep {B_nameDef} busy
li.outcome: The council handed {B_nameDef} a project big enough to fill the evenings, and {B_nameDef} works at it late, alone.
li.riskOutcome: The council handed {B_nameDef} a project to fill the evenings, and {B_nameDef} poured everything into it. This week {B_nameDef} has had the look of someone onto a good idea.

li.label: Leave them to it
li.outcome: The council stayed out of it. {A_nameDef} has new friends now, and {B_nameDef} has an empty seat at dinner.
li.riskOutcome: The council stayed out of it. {B_nameDef} went to bed straight after dinner and didn't come out again.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} and {B_possessive} friends have claimed the best table and the warm corner, and they go quiet whenever {A_nameDef} walks in. None of them has been rude, exactly, which makes it hard to complain about.\n\n{A_nameDef} is complaining anyway, and wants the council to break the circle open. {B_nameDef} says who {B_pronoun} sits with is {B_possessive} own business.

There's a group in this colony that eats together, works together and laughs at jokes no one else understands. {A_nameDef} isn't in it, and {B_nameDef}, who can't stand {A_nameDef}, is most of the reason why.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council to do something about it. {B_nameDef} wants to know since when friendship needs the council's permission.

li.label: Order them to make room for {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: By order of the council, {A_nameDef} now has a seat at the circle's table. They pass {A_objective} the bread and talk around {A_objective} as if the seat were empty.
li.riskOutcome: By order of the council, {A_nameDef} got a seat at the circle's table and turned out to be funnier than anyone expected. Even {B_nameDef} laughed once, and looked furious about it afterward.

li.label: Mix up the work crews
li.outcome: The council broke up the work crews and shuffled everyone. The circle is scattered across the colony now, and its members are bitter about it.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} host a supper for everyone
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} hosted a supper for the colony, and people came, even some of the circle. {A_nameDef} was still smiling the next morning.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} hosted a supper for the whole colony. {B_nameDef} threw a party of {B_possessive} own the same night, and most of the chairs at {A_nameDef}'s table stayed empty.

li.label: Let people choose their own friends
li.outcome: The council ruled that no one can be ordered to like anyone. {B_nameDef} agreed warmly, and {A_nameDef} ate dinner alone again.
li.riskOutcome: The council ruled that no one can be ordered to like anyone. {A_nameDef} walked out of the meeting and didn't come back until dark.

texts.li: The colony finally has a storeroom the rain doesn't get into, and the harvest keeps better for it. {A_nameDef} says the idea and most of the labor were {A_possessive}. {B_nameDef} says they were {B_possessive}.\n\nEach wants the council to say publicly whose work it was, and each is sure the other is lying.

The new defenses on the east side are the best work the colony has done all season. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} both claim the design, and both have the calluses to prove they did the labor.\n\nThey've asked the council to settle it. Both have hinted that they'll take a wrong answer badly.

li.label: Credit {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: The council named {A_nameDef} as the builder. {A_nameDef} has been showing it off to anyone who'll stop, and {B_nameDef} has been finding somewhere else to be.
li.riskOutcome: The council named {A_nameDef} as the builder, and {B_nameDef} went for {A_objective} at the next meal.

li.label: Credit {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: The council named {B_nameDef} as the builder. {B_nameDef} brings it up at every chance, and {A_nameDef} has stopped speaking to {B_objective}.
li.riskOutcome: The council named {B_nameDef} as the builder. {A_nameDef} found {B_nameDef} in the yard that evening, and the two of them fought over it.

li.label: Carve both their names on it
li.outcome: The council credited them jointly and carved both names into it. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} grumbled, but the arguing has mostly stopped.
li.riskOutcome: The council had both names carved into it. By evening {A_nameDef} had scratched out {B_nameDef}'s name, and the two of them came to blows over it.

li.label: Credit the colony as a whole
li.outcome: The council ruled that the work belongs to the colony, not to anyone in it. Neither {A_nameDef} nor {B_nameDef} thinks that's fair, and both have said so.
li.riskOutcome: The council ruled it was colony work. Somebody carved {A_nameDef}'s name into it that night, and somebody else carved over it by morning.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} broke one of the council's standing orders, openly, in front of witnesses. The punishment ought to be simple. But {B_nameDef} came to the council last night and begged for mercy on {A_possessive} behalf, and {B_nameDef} doesn't beg.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants {A_nameDef} spared. Several others want to know whether the rules bend for people with good friends.

{A_nameDef} broke the rules this week and hasn't tried to deny it. Then {B_nameDef} turned up at the council's door at dawn, asking to speak for {A_objective}.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants mercy. Most of the colony wants the rules to mean something.

li.label: Show mercy
li.outcome: The council spared {A_nameDef} on {B_nameDef}'s word. {A_nameDef} knows whom to thank. Some of the others think the council plays favorites.

li.label: Punish {A_nameDef} as the rules say
li.outcome: The council heard {B_nameDef} out, then punished {A_nameDef} anyway. {B_nameDef} has decided the council's door isn't worth knocking on again.

li.label: Halve it, if {B_nameDef} takes the other half
li.outcome: The council halved the punishment and handed the other half to {B_nameDef}. The two of them are working it off together, and don't seem to mind.

li.label: Double it, for trying to sway the council
li.outcome: The council doubled {A_nameDef}'s punishment for the attempt to sway it. {A_nameDef} hasn't said a word to {B_nameDef} since, and {B_nameDef} hasn't stopped apologizing.
li.riskOutcome: The council doubled {A_nameDef}'s punishment for the attempt to sway it. {B_nameDef} walked out of the hearing and kept walking, out past the fields.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} has been watching the stores, and says the quartermaster's friends do better than everyone else: the fine meals, the warm coats, first pick of every trade. The quartermaster is {A_nameDef}, whom {B_nameDef} has despised for a long time.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants {A_nameDef} called to account. {A_nameDef} says {B_nameDef} would find favoritism in a bowl of plain rice.

{B_nameDef} brought the council a list of every extra ration, new coat and good bed that has gone to {A_nameDef}'s friends since {A_nameDef} took the quartermaster's keys. Some of it is true. Some of it looks like the work of a rival with time on {B_possessive} hands.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants the keys taken away. {A_nameDef} wants the list thrown on the fire.

li.label: Audit the stores
li.outcome: The council counted every sack and coat in the stores, and it all added up. {A_nameDef} is offended to have been checked at all, and {B_nameDef} refuses to accept the count.
li.riskOutcome: The council counted the stores and found the list was mostly true. {A_nameDef} was taken down a peg in front of the colony, and the quartermaster's friends now eat the same as everyone else.

li.label: Back the quartermaster
li.outcome: The council backed {A_nameDef} without reading the list. The quartermaster's friends were relieved. {B_nameDef} now says the council is in on it.

li.label: Make {B_nameDef} keep the ledger
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} now checks every ration {A_nameDef} hands out and writes it down. Handing out supplies takes twice as long, but no one can call it unfair.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} now checks every ration {A_nameDef} hands out. On the second day the two of them argued over a single potato, and it came to blows.

li.label: Hand out the good things by lot
li.outcome: The council took the choosing out of {A_nameDef}'s hands. From now on, the good things go by drawing lots. Some people have done well out of it, and the quartermaster's friends have not.
